title: Mirai Botnet Investigation
description: Investigate a network compromised by the Mirai botnet variant Linux/Mirai-Hilix. Identify the beacon service communicating with the C2 server, the flood service responsible for DDoS attacks, and the persistence mechanism ensuring the malware's continued operation.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Unix/Linux systemd services
Basic knowledge of Linux system administration

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has been experiencing unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of these issues. The network consists of several Linux-based systems, including a command-and-control server (c2-server), two potential compromised hosts (bot1 and bot2), and a victim server (victim). All systems are running Ubuntu Noble.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the entry host bot1 with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.

levels.title: Identify the Suspicious Beacon Service
levels.content: Investigate the services running on bot1 and identify the service responsible for beaconing to the C2 server. The flag is the name of the service.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services. The service name is bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Beaconing services typically communicate with a command-and-control server at regular intervals.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for services that might be communicating with external servers.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

levels.title: Identify the Suspicious Flood Service
levels.content: Examine the services on bot1 and find the service that is generating flood traffic. The flag is the name of the service.
levels.solution: Look for services related to network diagnostics or similar descriptions. The service name is bot-flood-Hilix.sh.service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Flood services typically generate excessive network traffic to overwhelm target systems.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for services that might be generating high volumes of network traffic.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

levels.title: Identify and Remove the Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigate the systemd timers and services to find and remove the persistence mechanism that ensures the malware runs after reboots. The flag is the name of the timer.
levels.solution: Check the systemd timers and look for any suspicious timers that might be related to the malware. The timer name is system-update-checker.timer.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms often use systemd timers to ensure malware runs after system reboots.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for timers that might be triggering the execution of suspicious services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check the systemd timers and look for any suspicious timers that might be related to the malware.
